data.narrative:
Hyperscale Power is a seed-stage Climate & Energy company founded by Daniel Rothmund (PhD ETH Zürich, former ABB) and Sami Pettersson (ex-ABB), having raised €5M to date. The broader sector comprises 9 private peers and 1 public comparable (Lonza, LNZA), though the seed-stage cohort is sparse within this universe.

Peer-median valuation proved inapplicable: the Climate & Energy sector contains only one public company and eight private peers, but filtering for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier companies yielded fewer than three datapoints in each category. A median derived from the full sector would obscure material differences in stage, technology maturity, and capital intensity. Top private comparables—Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen—span substantially later stages and higher valuations, limiting direct inference.

Without sufficient narrow peer coverage, conventional triangulation methods do not yield a defensible valuation range. A credible assessment would require either: (1) deeper diligence into the target's unit economics, technology differentiation, and market sizing relative to the broader Climate & Energy landscape; (2) application of DCF or venture capital method frameworks anchored to explicit assumptions about go-to-market trajectory; or (3) expansion of the comp set to include adjacent infrastructure or industrial technology seed-stage exits. Current data supports only the observation that seed-stage Climate & Energy companies are underrepresented in public markets and clustered at higher valuation tiers post-seed.
